texts.preamble: State vs . Mukul Singh on 9 March, 2023 In The Court Of Sh. Pranav Joshi Metropolitan Magistrate03, North, Rohini Courts, Delhi State Vs. Mukul Singh Fir No. 169/2011 Ps K.N.K. Marg U/s. 279/3337/338 Ipc Cis No. 5287732/2016 Judgment
texts.facts: THE BRIEF REASONS FOR THE JUDGMENT: 1. Briefly stated the case of the prosecution is that on 21.4.2011 at about 11.15 pm at E Block, Sector 15. Rohini, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS KNK Marg, the accused was driving a TATA Indica bearing No. DL 8CM 2612 on a public way in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and personal safety of others and he struck against one scooter no. DL 8SV 7749 as a result of which Sh. Tushar Ahuja received simple injuries and Sh. Puneet received grievous injuries. He was chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Section 279/337/338 IPC. State vs . Mukul Singh on 9 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12061482/ 1 2. After completion of investigation, chargesheet for the offences under section 279/337/338 IPC was filed against the accused whereupon cognizance was taken. After complying with the provisions of Sec. 207 Cr. P.C , arguments on charge were heard and vide order dated 20.01.2012, notice was served to the accused for offence u/s 279/337/338 IPC to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 3. The prosecution examined eight witnesses. PW Raj Kumar deposed that he did not remember the date of incident. On the day of incident, accident happened with his nephew Tushar Ahuja and his friend Puneet Raj. He deposed that they were hit by car which was driven by accused Mukul. The accused fled from the spot after accident. Thereafter, they filed a complaint against the accused. He identified the accused as well as the photographs of the offending vehicle correctly. He was recalled for his further examination on 26.11.2010 wherein he stated that on 21/04/2011, at about 11:10 p.m., his nephew Tushar along with his friend Puneet came down together from second floor, his nephew was going on his scooter along with his friend Puneet to get food from Vishram Chowk. While they were starting the scooter, PW1 had reached the dividing road near Pan Shop. He heard noise of an accident, in front of the gate of G Block, Sector 15, Rohini. He along with other persons, reached the place and he saw that it was his nephew who had met with accident. He saw the boy who had caused the accident, trying to flee the spot. He had caused the accident with Indica Car. He along with Puneet took his nephew to Satyam Hospital for first aid. After first aid, they took his nephew to BSA Hospital. He called 100 number. After some time, Mukul's father came to BSA Hospital. IO also reached the hospital and recorded his statement. He stated that he did not want to proceed with the case. The witness was cross examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused 4. PW Sh. Bajrang Singh deposed that he was the registered owner of car DLBC M2612. At the time of incident on 21.04.11, the said car was in the possession of his son who is accused in the present case. He had replied to the notice u/s. 133 MV Act vide Ex.PW2/A. He deposed that on 27.04.11, he had produced the RC and insurance of the above said car to the IO which was seized by him vide memo Ex.PW2/B. He released the said car on superdari vide superdarinama Ex.PW2/C. Witness brought the offending car Ex.P 1. The witness was not crossexamined by Ld. Counsel for the accused despite opportunity being given. 5. PW Sh. Puneet Raj deposed that On 21.04.2011, he was studying in 12th standard. On that day, he was present at the house No. B2/89, Sec16. Rohini Delhi of his friend Tusar Ahuja (since deceased). On that day at about 11.15 pm, he along with his friend Tusar Ahuja had left house for taking dinner from Vishram Chowk on scooter No. DL8SV7749. He deposed that he was driving the scooter and when they reached in front of the Gate of E Block, Sec15, Rohini, the offending Tata Indica Car bearing DL 8CM 2612 came from the side of Manav Chowk towards EBlock, which was being driven by the accused Mukul in a very rash and zig zag manner and in a high speed. While turning his car towards E block, the accused hit his car against their scooter from right side and caused the accident. Due to the impact, he and his friend Tushar fell down on the road along with the scooter. Sh. Raj Kumar Ahuja, uncle (chacha) of Tusar who was sitting nearby Pan shop immediately came to the spot after seeing the accident. Raj Kumar Ahuja had apprehended the accused Mukul at the spot with the offending vehicle. He along with Tushar were shifted to the BSA Hospital in the offending vehicle of the accused where we were medically examined. They were State vs . Mukul Singh on 9 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12061482/ 2 referred to Satyam Hospital from BSA Hospital. Father of the accused came to the Satyam hospital. He came to know about the name of the accused of the offending vehicle as Mukul in the hospital. He received fracture on his right leg and sustained grievous injuries. His statement was recorded by the IO on 30.08.2011 at the Police Station. The witness correctly identified the accused in the court. The witness was shown to the photographs of the offending vehicle. The witness identified the handwriting of injured Tushar (since he has expired) at statement of Tushar Ahuja Ex.PW3/A, site plan Ex.PW3/B, seizure memo of scooter Ex.PW3/C, seizure memo of car Ex.PW3/D and arrest memo Ex.PW3/E. The witness was not crossexamined by the accused despite opportunity being given. 6. PW HC Hari Om deposed that on 21.04.2011, he was posted as constable at KNK Marg. On that day, he was on duty as DD writer and his duty timings were from 4:00 pm to 12:00 mid night. At about 11:50 pm. wireless operator informed him about an accident near Satyam Hospital Sec16. Rohini, Delhi. He recorded the same vide DD No. 100B to the DD register in his own handwriting. He brought the original DD register containing the said entry. The true copy of the same placed was on record as Ex. PW 4/A (OSR). 7. PW HC Rajender Singh deposed that On 21.04.2011 22.04.2011, he was posted as Head Constable at PS. KNK Marg. On that day, he was working as a duty officer and his duty hours were from 12 Mid Night to 8 AM. On 22.04.2011, at about 1:25 AM, a rukka was brought by constable Ravinder which was sent by IO SI Rajesh for getting the case registered. On the basis of rukka, he registered the present FIR through CIPA operator under his supervision and the computer system worked properly and nothing adverse happened in the system during that time. He brought the original register containing the FIR No. 169/11 and computerized copy of the same EXPW5/A (OSR). He also made endorsement on original rukka Ex. PW5/B. Thereafter, he handed over the original rukka and copy of FIR to Ct. Ravinder for further handing to IO. The witness was not cross examined by the accused despite opportunity being given. 8. PW Dr. Deepti Bhalla deposed that on 22.04.2011, she was posted at Dr. B.S.A. Hospital as CMO. On that day patient namely Puneet aged about 22 years brought in the casualty with the alleged history of RTA by PCR official namely ASI Sarju Singh. She medically examined the patient and found that patient was conscious oriented. His vitals were stable. She deposed that smell of alcohol was present in his breath and Patient was complaining of pain and swelling over the right leg at that time. She found diffuse swelling and tenderness over the right leg of the patient, deformity restriction of movement and multiple abrasion over the left hand, left wrist right foot and right heel on the patient. She deposed that per the MLC patient had already received primary treatment from Satyam Hospital, Rohini. She deposed that at BSA casualty his X ray of right leg was done and the patient was referred to SR Ortho for expert opinion and further management. She declared the patient as fit for statement on same date at 12:30 a.m. She further deposed that she prepared the MLC No. 3035/11 dated 22.04.2011 Ex PW 5/A. On 22.04.2011, patient namely Tushar Ahuja, aged about 18 years brought in the casualty with the alleged history of RTA by PCR official namely ASI Sarju Singh. Dr. Ashish (JR Casualty) medically examined the patient under her supervision and found that patient was conscious oriented. She deposed that Dr. Ashish State vs . Mukul Singh on 9 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12061482/ 3 prepared the MLC No. 3034/11 dated 22.04.2011 Ex. PW 5/B. Dr. Ashish opined the nature of injuries as simple. She identified the writing and signatures of Dr. Ashish as she had worked with him during the course of their duties. 9. PW Ct. Ravinder deposed that on 21.04.2011, he was posted at PS KNK Marg as a constable. On that day he was on emergency duty from 8:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. On that day DD no. 100 B was marked to SI Rajesh. After receiving the information he accompanied SI Rajesh and went to Satyam Hospital. At Satyam hospital, they did not find any eye witness/complainant/injured. Thereafter, IO SI Rajesh came to know through telephone of the caller of 100 number that the injured has been shifted to BSA Hospital. Thereafter, they visited BSA Hospital and found two injured persons were admitted in the hospital, whose name revealed as Tushar Ahuja and Puneet. At that time complainant/injured stated to the IO that the offending vehicle bearing no. DL 8C M 2612, make TATA Indica was parked in front of emergency ward of the hospital. At hospital IO collected the MLC of the injured person. Accused/driver namely Mukul Singh Shekhawat was present in the hospital. Complainant/injured Tushar had given his complaint to the IO, IO recorded the same information vide Ex. PW 3/A. After the preparation of the rukka, IO handed over the same to him to registration of FIR at PS. Accordingly, he went to the PS to get the FIR registered. Meanwhile, IO along with the complainant and offending vehicle reached at PS. Thereafter, he along with IO, complainant, accused went to the spot i.e. EBlock, Sector 15, Rohini and at the instance of the complainant, IO prepared site plan Ex. PW 3/B. He put his signature on the seizure memo of scooty bearing registration no. DL 8S V 7749 Ex. PW 3/C. Aforesaid scooty was parked at the place of incident in the accidental condition. At the hospital another injured Puneet was seriously injured. At that time IO did not collect the MLC of the injured Tushar as it was incomplete. He narrated the whole incident to the IO and IO recorded his statement. During the investigation, IO prepared the relevant documents. The witness identified the accused and the photographs of the vehicle correctly. The witness was cross examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused. 10. PW SI Gurjant Singh deposed that on 10.07.2011, he was posted at PS KNK Marg as ASI. On that day he had received the case file of the present case through MHCR. During the investigation, he verified the documents i.e. insurance and DL and same were found genuine. He deposed that investigation was mostly conducted by the previous IO SI Rajesh Kumar. After the completion of the investigation, he filed the charge sheet of the present case. The witness was crossexamined by Ld. Counsel for the accused. 11. PW SI Rajesh Kumar deposed that on 21.04.2011, he was posted at PS KNK Marg as SI. On that day, he was on emergency duty along with Ct. Ravinder. At around 11:15 p.m., he received the DD no. 100B Ex. PW 4/A regarding the accident. After receiving the same, he along with Ct. Ravinder reached at spot i.e. near the Satyam Hospital, divider road, Sector 15 and 16. After reaching there he found nothing at the spot. Thereafter, he got the information about the caller from PCR office. He made a call at caller number and then he came to know that injured had gone to BSA Hospital for medical treatment. Thereafter, he reached at BSA Hospital along with the constable Ravinder. He collected the MLC of the injured Tushar Ahuja. At that time the MLC of the another injured namely Puneet was not prepared by the concerned doctor. He recorded the statement of State vs . Mukul Singh on 9 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12061482/ 4 injured/complainant Tushar Ahuja, who was fit for the statement Ex. PW3/A. He made the endorsement on the complaint and handed over the rukka to Ct. Ravinder and sent him for the registration of FIR at PS. In the parking of the BSA Hospital, complainant Tushar Ahuja identified offending vehicle. He seized the same vehicle vide seizure memo of the car bearing registration no. DL. 8CM 2612 Ex. PW 3/D. He had given the direction to Ct. Ravinder to remain at the PS after the registration of FIR. Thereafter, He along with the offending vehicle reached at PS. Meanwhile, complainant reached at the PS through the vehicle of his uncle. He collected the FIR and original rukka from Ct. Ravinder. He along with the complainant/injured Tushar Ahuja reached at spot i.e. Eblock, Sector 15, Rohini. Complainant had shown the place of incident to him and he prepared the site plan Ex. PW 3/B at the instance of the complainant. At that time complainant also stated that accidental scooter is parked in front of his house. Thereafter, he along with complainant reached at the house of the complainant i.e. B2/89, Sector 16, Rohini, from there he seized the accidental scooter bearing registration no. DL 8SV 7749 vide seizure memo Ex. PW 3/C. He recorded the supplementary statement of the complainant and his uncle. He deposited the accidental scooter of the complainant in the malkhana of the PS. During the investigation, he moved the application Ex. A1 (colly) for mechanical inspection of both the accidental vehicles i.e. scooter and car. He served notice upon the registered owner of offending car Ex.PW 2/A. At that time registered owner Bajrang Singh gave the reply of the notice. Registered owner also visited at PS after receiving the notice, however, accused was not produced by him at that time. He seized the RC and insurance from the registered owner vide seizure memo Ex. PW 2/B. In the reply of the notice U/s 133 MV Act, registered owner stated that on the day of the incident, accused Mukul was driving the offending car. During the investigation he collected and took the opinion on the MLC of both the injured namely Puneet and Tushar Ahuja. As per the MLC, section 338 was added in the charge sheet. On 17.05.2011, accused Mukul was produced by the registered owner. He seized the licence of the accused vide seizure memo Ex. PW 8/A. He arrested the accused at PS vide arrest memo Ex. PW 3/E. At that time complainant also visited at PS to inquire about his matter. At that time complainant identified the accused who was present in the PS and stated that accused had committed the accident. He did not record the statement of the another injured Puneet as he was not available. The statement of the another injured was recorded by the last IO ASI Gurjant Singh. He was transferred during the investigation, therefore, he handed over the case file to concerned MHCR. Accused as well as the photographs of the case property was correctly identified by the witness. 12. During the course of trial on 12.07.2019 and19.08.2019, the accused made a statement u/s 294 Cr.P.C and admitted the mechanical inspection report Ex. A1, genuineness of the MLC No. 3035/11, MLC NO. 3034/11 along with XRay report No. 1096 and XRay plate Ex. A2 (colly) and the relevant entries of register No. 19 and 21 of MHCM Ex. A3. Hence, the concerned witness were not called for proving these documents. 13. The prosecution could not examine injured/PW Tushar Ahuja as he expired during the pendency of trial. 14. Statement of the accused under section 313 Cr.P.C was recorded, wherein accused pleaded innocence and false implication in the present case. Accused opted not to lead defence evidence.
texts.arguments: In this regard, it is relevant to reproduce the observations made by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kali Ram Vs. Himanchal Pradesh (1973 2 SCC 808) in para 23 and 25 which are reproduced as under: " 23. Observations in a recent decision of this Court, Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade & Anr. v. State of Maharashtra (1973 2 SCC 793) to which reference has been made during arguments were not intended to make a departure from the rule of the presumption of innocence of the accused and his entitlement to the benefit of reasonable doubt in criminal cases. One of the cardinal principles which has always to be kept in view in our system of administration of justice for criminal cases is that a person arraigned as an accused is presumed to be innocent unless that presumption is rebutted by the prosecution by production of evidence as may show him to be guilty of the offence with which he is charged. It is also an accepted rule that in case the 73 5 court entertains reasonable doubt regarding the, guilt of the accused, the State vs . Mukul Singh on 9 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12061482/ 6 accused must have the benefit of that doubt. As mentioned by us recently in the case of State of Punjab v. Jagir Singh,(1974 2 SCC 227) a criminal trial is not like a fairy tale wherein one is free to give flight to one's imagination and fantasy. It concerns itself with the question as to whether the accused arraigned at the trial is guilty of the offence with which he is charged. Crime is an event in real life and is the product of interplay of different human emotions. In arriving at the conclusion about the guilt of the accused charged with the commission of a crime, the, court has to judge, the evidence by the yardstick of probabilities, its intrinsic worth and the animus of witnesses. Although the benefit of every reasonable doubt should be given to the accused, the courts should not at the same time reject evidence which is ex facie trustworthy, on grounds which are fanciful or in the nature of conjectures." Section 279 IPC reads as under : 279. Rash driving or riding on a public way.--Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Section 337 IPC reads as under : 337. Causing hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others. Whoever causes hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both. Section 338 IPC reads as under : State vs . Mukul Singh on 9 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12061482/ 7 338. Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
